rows.scope: New Hampshire, five years pooled, 2018-2022: the share of unintentional injury deaths of children (printed as 'among children between the ages of 1 to 21'; the report defines children as birth to 21 on p. 4) that the NH Child Fatality Review Committee's report attributes to drowning (chart label 'Drowning (8.1%)', Figure 4, section 'Unintentional Injury Deaths'). Death-certificate data (NH Vital Records). A percentage only: no count, series, setting or ICD codes printed. Adults not covered. Year is the end of the period.
rows.source: NH DHHS, Child Fatality Review Committee, Annual Report 2023 (data from NH DHHS Health Statistics and Data Management, death certificates from the NH Division of Vital Records Administration), p. 11
rows.do_not_add_to: A pooled five-year share for children, not a count: never multiply it by any total in this ledger (us-cdc-4345, us-cdc-4500, us-total-2022) to make a New Hampshire count, never add it to uscg-boating-2024 or us-location-boating-2024, and never combine it with the canada-location-*, australia-location-2024-25 or uk-waid-2024 shares, whose denominators are drowning deaths by setting, not injury deaths of children. Not the yearly all-ages NH count this task asked for.
rows.note: The only New Hampshire drowning figure found in an official document the tools could open. The Executive Summary (p. 1) ranks drowning third among the top six causes of preventable child death for 2018-2022, after motor vehicles and poisoning/overdose. Yearly all-ages counts sit behind CDC WONDER, WISQARS and NH Health WISDOM and were not read. A reviewer should check p. 11 by eye: the text's '(Figure 4)' cross-reference collides with the p. 10 homicide chart titled Figure 4, the denominator N is image-only, and the six printed shares sum to 85.3%. Found 21 Oct 2026.

notes: Result: no yearly, all-ages count of drowning deaths for New Hampshire was found in any document the tools could open, so the task's central acceptance point is not met. The three sources that hold such counts each need a person with a browser: CDC WONDER (data-use agreement), CDC WISQARS (JavaScript app, no agreement seen) and the NH Health WISDOM Injury Prevention Dashboard (JavaScript app). The NH OCME's only public report (2017-2019) has no drowning line, and no NH vital-statistics cause table was found online. What was found: one official NH drowning figure, a pooled 2018-2022 share of child unintentional-injury deaths (8.1%) from the NH DHHS Child Fatality Review report, recorded as a share with a strict do-not-add rule. The reviewer should open p. 11 of that PDF by eye: the reading tool described Figure 4 as covering ages 1 to 21 while the report defines children as birth to 21, and the tool could not reproduce the chart. The reading tool also offered its own arithmetic estimate of a child drowning count from that share; it is not in the report and is not recorded anywhere in this bundle. Correction: the ledger row us-cdc-4345 (4,345 a year, 2018-2021, 'CDC, Drowning data (27 Jan 2026)') cites /drowning/data/index.html, which as fetched today prints 'over 4,000' a year and an average of 4,083 for 2012-2021 (data accessed 31 May 2023); the 4,345 figure with the 27 Jan 2026 review date is on /drowning/data-research/index.html, so the url is proposed as the correction. One caveat: the /data/ page may be an older copy served from a cache, and only that older page says the figure includes boating-related drowning; a reviewer should open both pages. Deliberately left out: the USCG 2024 report's Table 8 New Hampshire row (alcohol-related boating incidents, deaths and injuries 2020-2024), because it is not a drowning count and is a subset by contributing factor. No press figure was used. Roughly 37 searches and fetches were spent, above the suggested 25, because the OCME, DHHS, Marine Patrol, Fish and Game, Vital Records, CDC and USCG routes each had to be checked before saying not found. Quotes are 12 words or fewer and one per document, per the brief.
